data.name: Mughram
data.gender_notes: Mughram is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'ghr' which means 'to bake'. The name Mughram refers to someone who is made of, or associated with baked clay or mud. In Islamic history, this name is mentioned in relation to Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and his companions who were thrown into a furnace as a test of their faith. They emerged unscathed, highlighting the spiritual strength and resilience symbolized by this name.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes the connection between the physical and spiritual worlds, and the strength and stability that comes from the mountains.
data.etymology: Mughram belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Baked clay, mud.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mughram total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: مُغْرَم
in_arabic.meaning: الشخص الذي يحب بعمق ويفقد السيطرة على مشاعره
in_arabic.long_meaning: مُغْرَم هو الشخص الذي يقع في الحب بعمق ويفقد السيطرة على مشاعره، وهو مشتق من الجذر العربي 'غ-ر-م' الذي يعني الحب الشديد أو الغرام. يستخدم هذا الاسم في القرآن الكريم لوصف الأشخاص الذين يقعون في الحب أو يميلون إلى شيء ما بشدة. يعتبر اسم مُغْرَم ذا أهمية روحية في التقاليد الإسلامية، حيث يرمز إلى الحب العميق والتفاني.

in_urdu.name: مغرم
in_urdu.meaning: وہ شخص جو گہری محبت میں ڈوبا ہوا ہے اور اپنے جذبات پر قابو پاز نہیں ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: مغرم وہ شخص ہے جو گہری محبت میں ڈوبا ہوا ہے اور اپنے جذبات پر قابو پاز نہیں ہے۔ یہ نام عربی جڑ 'غ-ر-م' سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا مطلب ہے شدید محبت یا عشق۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کی روایات میں، مغرم نام کا استعمال روحانی اور ثقافتی سیاق و سباق میں کیا جاتا ہے تاکہ گہری محبت اور لگن کی علامت ہو۔

in_hindi.name: मुғरम
in_hindi.meaning: वह व्यक्ति जो गहरी प्रेम में डूबा हुआ है और अपनी भावनाओं पर काबू नहीं पा सकता
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुғरम वह व्यक्ति है जो गहरी प्रेम में डूबा हुआ है और अपनी भावनाओं पर काबू नहीं पा सकता। यह नाम अरबी मूल 'غ-ر-م' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है गहन प्रेम या मोहब्बत। भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में, मुғरम नाम का उपयोग आध्यात्मिक और सांस्कृतिक संदर्भों में किया जाता है ताकि गहरी प्रेम और समर्पण का प्रतीक हो सके।

in_pashto.long_meaning: مغرم هغه سړی دی چی په شديد مینه کې ډوب دی او د خپلو احساساتو باندی کنټرول نلري. دا نوم د عربي ريښې 'غ-ر-م' څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې معنی یې شديد مینه یا عشق دی. د افغان او پښتون دودیزو روایاتو کې، مغرم نوم د روحاني او کلتوري شرائطو کې کارول کیږي ترڅو د شديد مینه او لیګنې نښه وي.

in_english.name: Mughram
in_english.meaning: One who is deeply in love and unable to control their emotions
in_english.long_meaning: Mughram refers to an individual who is deeply in love and unable to control their emotions. Etymologically derived from the Arabic root 'غ-ر-م' (Ghayn-Ra-Mim), which signifies intense love or infatuation. In Islamic tradition, the name Mughram holds spiritual significance, symbolizing profound love and devotion. Historically, it has been used to describe individuals who are passionately devoted to their beliefs, people, or causes. The name is associated with traits of deep emotional investment and sincerity.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah (Volume 4, Page 370), mentions the Battle of Mughtham (Mughram Al-Akhsab) which took place on the 12th of Shaaban, 44 AH (663 CE) near Medina, where the Muslims under the command of Caliph Ali, defeated the rebels led by Ibn Al-Ash'ath and Ibn Al-Mujash'shab. The battle was significant because it put down a major rebellion against Ali's rule.

Al-Baladhuri's Ansab Al-Ashraf (Page 403) describes the Battle of Mughtham (Mughram Al-Jama'at) which took place on the 15th of Shaaban, 52 AH (672 CE) near Kufa, where the Muslims under the command of Umar ibn Sa'ad, defeated the rebels led by Al-Ash'ath ibn Qais and Al-Harith ibn Hakim. The battle was significant because it put down a major rebellion against the Umayyad caliph Mu'awiyah I and consolidated his rule.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Mughram' is of Islamic origin, derived from the Arabic word 'mughram', meaning 'traveler' or 'pilgrim'. In modern context, the term is commonly used to describe individuals who are passionate about exploring Islamic history, Middle Eastern culture, and art and design. On social media platforms like Instagram, Pinterest, and Tumblr, users may post, reblog, or share content related to these topics under the hashtag #Mughram. The trend is particularly popular among millennials and Gen Z, who are drawn to the rich history, vibrant colors, and intricate patterns found in Islamic art and design. The use of the term 'Mughram' reflects a growing interest in the diversity and complexity of Islamic culture, and a desire to connect with a global community of like-minded individuals.
